angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,835,952 km at 55.87 pc = 0.44 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 105140: distance 55.866 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.013), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 55.866 +/- 0.726 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 19.2981 +/- 0.2671 mas (same row, RUWE 2.24), 72.2 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 2.639 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 105140: radius 2.639 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 31.77 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.283) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 1,835,952 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 8442 +/- 1273 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 105140: effective temperature 8442 +/- 1273 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.052) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 105140: effective temperature 8442 +/- 1273 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.052) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * eps Mic: spectral type A0V (1982MSS...C03....0H)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * eps Mic: projected rotation speed 110 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
